title: Fossil Forgotten in a Museum Drawer Reveals a New Dinosaur
summary:
A dinosaur fossil that sat almost unnoticed in a museum for nearly 100 years has turned out to be a brand-new species. The predator lived about 120 million years ago in what is now Britain.

Scientists led by University College London (UCL) studied a piece of the back of a dinosaur skull found on the Isle of Wight, an island off England's southern coast. London's Natural History Museum got the fossil in 1924, but no one realized how important it was.

The researchers named the dinosaur Invictibellatrix amberina. The name means "unconquered female warrior." It belongs to a mysterious group of meat-eating dinosaurs called megaraptorans. They walked on two legs and were related to Tyrannosaurus rex. But instead of using giant jaws, megaraptorans had narrow skulls, strong arms and huge curved claws for catching food.

Lead author Dr. Cassius Morrison said the dinosaur was probably three to four meters long and about as tall as a person. It likely had feathers, and its claws may have been 10 to 20 centimeters long. It probably ate small dinosaurs, lizards and mammals. Morrison noted that a human would have been the right size prey for this hunter, while a T. rex would not have bothered. Of course, people and dinosaurs never lived at the same time.

The fossil also solves a puzzle. Scientists thought megaraptorans first appeared in Asia and then spread through Europe to southern lands such as Africa and South America. But no megaraptoran had ever been found in Europe until now.

"This new species is the first proof we have that megaraptorans were also present in Europe," said UCL student Charlie Scherer.

Morrison said many bones are found on the Isle of Wight. "Who knows what else is waiting to be discovered," he said.
why_it_matters: The discovery fills a gap in the story of how a mysterious group of dinosaurs spread across the world, and shows that old museum collections can still hold surprises.

background_read: Museums store huge collections of fossils, and some are not studied closely until many years after they are found.
Scientists can identify a new dinosaur from just part of a skeleton by comparing its shape with fossils of related animals.
Megaraptorans were meat-eating dinosaurs related to Tyrannosaurus rex, but they caught food with strong arms and large curved claws rather than giant jaws.
Because their fossils are rare, scientists have had trouble working out where megaraptorans first lived and how they spread to lands such as Africa and South America.
